p: If you've got a toddler and an older sibling, a little strategy helps. Bigger kids tend to charge about at full tilt, so it's worth keeping littler ones close and steering them towards the gentler areas while the older ones tackle the big obstacles. Ask the team about age guidance and any quieter sessions when you book, as some inflatable parks set times aside for younger children.

Comfy clothing without zips or buckles is the way to go, along with grip socks, hair tied back and jewellery left at home. Arrive a few minutes early so the shoes-and-coats faff doesn't eat into your slot, and have a drink ready for the end.

Cheltenham and its surroundings are packed with lovely places to round off the day. The Wilson, the town's art gallery and museum, is free to visit and has changing exhibitions plus a collection linked to the Arts and Crafts movement. The Holst Victorian House, birthplace of composer Gustav Holst, is a charming small museum. Head out of town and Cleeve Hill, the highest point in the Cotswolds, gives huge views across the Severn Vale, while Sudeley Castle near Winchcombe has beautiful gardens and a royal history linked to Katherine Parr. Racing fans will know Cheltenham Racecourse is just north of the town, with the famous Festival every March drawing huge crowds, so it's worth knowing those dates if you're planning a family trip and want quieter roads.
